Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 85, English)
A Collective Mantra Jaap Session: Sukshma Sharir Darshan and the Sangat's Meditation Experiences

This session is almost entir ely composed of live experience-sharing (anubhav) rather than conventional number ed teaching. As with prior live-practice sessions, Part I her e documents the practice's format and the r ecurring patterns/themes that emer ged acr oss dozens of individual accounts, rather than pr esenting doctrine in the usual style. Unlike the aura-checking sessions (82, 83), this session involves no negativity/pitru/tantra diagnosis — practitioners ar e voluntarily sharing positive meditative visions, so no anonymization has been applied; illustrative examples below ar e drawn fr om named accounts as given in the transcript.

1. Session Context and Starting Point The visible transcript opens mid-practice, with practitioners already completing their mala (rosary) count during a collective mantra jaap. Bhaiya instructs those who have finished to keep their jaap continuing informally while others catch up, rather than stopping abruptly .

2. The Submission (Samarpan) Instruction Once jaap is complete, practitioners are told to mentally submit (samarpit) their accumulated jaap at Baba's feet, using Bhaiya as a witness (saakshi). The prescribed inner prayer: "Prabhu, jo hamne abhi mantra jaap kiya hai, hum aapke charno mein samarpit karte hain — aap sweekar karo."

3. The Cor e Practice: A Split Subtle Body Reciting Two Mantras The central technique described across nearly every testimony is a dual mantra jaap using two subtle bodies (sukshma sharir) simultaneously — one side (commonly described as the left) reciting "Jai Siyaram" and the other side (commonly the right) reciting "Ram Ram," in parallel, with practitioners reporting they could hear or see both streams distinctly at once.

4. The Sharing Format After the jaap concludes, Bhaiya calls on practitioners one at a time by name to describe what they felt or saw (anubhav) during the practice, encouraging open, unfiltered sharing while others continue their own jaap quietly .

5. Recurring Pattern: Portals Opening A very common element across testimonies is the appearance of a portal (dwar/gate) — sometimes singular , sometimes multiple (one left, one right, one center) — through which ener gy , deities, or streams of saints are described entering or exiting.

6. Recurring Pattern: Color -Coded Energy and Subtle Bodies Practitioners frequently described their two subtle bodies as distinguishable by color — commonly white, gold, red, or blue — with the colors sometimes shifting or blending as the practice progressed, and ener gy described as visibly flowing from the hands, spine, or crown into the body .

7. Recurring Pattern: Divine Forms Appearing A wide range of deities and divine forms were reported across dif ferent practitioners' visions, including Ram and Sita, Hanuman ji, Shiv , Kali Mata (in one case appearing youthful, "16-17 saal ki," locked in battle with Mahishasur), Dur ga, Narsimha, and Ravana in his ten-headed (Dashanan) form during a Ram-Ravan battle scene.

8. Recurring Pattern: Baba/Guru Appearing Within the Vision Multiple practitioners reported seeing Baba (the guru) seated in their own place performing the jaap on their behalf, or saw their own subtle form transform mid-vision into Baba's form — described as a reassuring, unifying experience rather than a disorienting one.

9. Recurring Pattern: Saints (Sant) and Pr ocessions Several practitioners described encountering groups of saints — sometimes seated performing havan, sometimes walking in procession — who invited the practitioner to join them, occasionally leading to a sense of "traveling" through changing scenes toward a destination such as a forest ashram.

10. Recurring Pattern: Multiverse / Dimension-Shifting Visions More than one practitioner reported rapid shifts between many distinct scenes or "dimensions" within a single jaap session — one account described roughly 12-13 distinct dimensions witnessed in quick succession, including scenes of Mahishasur , Kali Mata, and Narsimha.

1 1. Recurring Pattern: Physical Sensations During Practice Reported physical sensations included tarang (waves/vibration) running through the body , a felt tightening or pressure (one practitioner compared it to sitting inside a pressure cooker), sudden fatigue or heaviness as if having run 100 meters, a feeling of floating or lightness, and eyes closing tightly and involuntarily during more intense visions.

12. Recurring Pattern: Energy Entering Through the Ears/Cr own Several practitioners specifically described seeing the words "Jai Siyaram" and "Ram" as visible text entering through their ears, or ener gy entering through the crown of the head, aligning with the sound of the mantra being recited.

13. Bhaiya's In-Session Clarification of the Dual-Mantra Mechanism Partway through the sharing, Bhaiya explicitly confirmed the pattern several practitioners were independently describing: that one side of the practitioner's awareness carries the "Jai Siyaram" stream while the other carries the "Ram" stream, audible or visible in parallel — validating this as a shared, real feature of the practice rather than an individual anomaly .

14. A Notable Testimony: The Locked Bathr oom One practitioner (Seema) shared that she had been accidentally locked in a bathroom by her family shortly before the session was due to start, and that as she prayed in distress to be let out in time, her daughter arrived and opened the door at exactly 9:00 — precisely when needed for the 9:30 session start. This was shared as a testimony of prayer being answered with striking, literal timing.

15. A Notable Observation: Aura Around Bhaiya The same practitioner also described continuously perceiving a white-colored aura around Bhaiya throughout the session, distinguishing it from simply the color of his clothing.

16. A Notable Testimony: Extended Multi-Scene Vision (Manam Lakshman Sir , Telangana) A practitioner from Telangana described an intense, rapidly escalating experience: ener gy entering like sunrise through the spine, an invisible subtle form chanting at high speed in an ancient temple setting, followed by a sensation of the body's ener gy "dividing" until it felt completely drained, likened to significant, sudden weight/ener gy loss.

17. Closing Teaching: Continuing Jaap During Dussehra Bhaiya closed the session by encouraging practitioners to continue their personal jaap that night for as long as their schedule allows — up to 12, 1, or 2 a.m. if possible, given the ongoing Dussehra festival period — while cautioning against overdoing it to the point of missing the next morning's work obligations; night-time jaap is encouraged where practical, but not at the cost of basic responsibilities.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

The core practice in this session is a collective mantra jaap in which two subtle bodies (sukshma sharir) each carry a dif ferent mantra — one "Jai Siyaram," the other "Ram" — recited in parallel. After jaap, practitioners submit their accumulated merit at Baba's feet, using Bhaiya as witness, rather than keeping the "credit" of the japa for themselves. Recurring elements across the sangat's shared visions include portals opening, color -coded twin subtle bodies, appearances of Ram-Sita, Hanuman, Shiv , Kali Mata, Dur ga, Narsimha, and Ravana, Baba appearing within the vision, processions of saints, multiverse/dimension-shifting scenes, and physical sensations like tarang, pressure, fatigue, or floating.

Bhaiya confirmed the dual-mantra, dual-subtle-body pattern as a real, shared feature of this practice, not an individual anomaly . This session contains no individual negativity/pitru/tantra diagnosis, so no privacy-based anonymization was required; named testimonies are reproduced as shared. Practitioners are encouraged to continue personal jaap into the night during the Dussehra period where their schedule allows, without compromising basic next-day responsibilities like work or waking on time. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 85, English)
A Collective Mantra Jaap Session: Sukshma Sharir Darshan and the Sangat's Meditation Experiences
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live collective mantra jaap and experience-sharing session.

Q1. What is the cor e practice described in this session? A: Per this teaching's live practice, the session centers on a collective mantra jaap in which practitioners visualize two subtle bodies (sukshma sharir), each reciting a dif ferent mantra in parallel — commonly "Jai Siyaram" on one side and "Ram" on the other .

Q2. What should a practitioner do with their jaap once their mala (r osary count) is complete? A: Per this teaching, once a practitioner's mala is complete, they mentally submit (samarpit) the accumulated jaap at Baba's feet, using Bhaiya as witness, with an inner prayer of fering the merit rather than retaining it personally , while continuing to sit quietly if others are still completing their own count.

Q3. What is the format for sharing experiences after the jaap? A: Per this teaching's live practice, after the jaap concludes, Bhaiya calls on practitioners one at a time by name to describe what they felt or saw during the practice, encouraging open sharing of both vivid visions and simple physical sensations.

Q4. What r ecurring visual element did many practitioners describe seeing during this practice? A: Per this teaching's live practice, a very common element was the appearance of one or more portals (dwar/gate), through which ener gy , deities, or processions of saints were described as entering or exiting.

Q5. Did practitioners r eport seeing specific deities during this practice? A: Yes — per this teaching's live practice, practitioners reported a wide range of divine forms, including Ram and Sita, Hanuman ji, Shiv , Kali Mata, Dur ga, Narsimha, and Ravana in his tenheaded (Dashanan) form, varying from person to person.

Q6. Did Baba (the guru) appear within practitioners' visions? A: Yes — per this teaching's live practice, multiple practitioners reported seeing Baba seated in their own place performing the jaap on their behalf, or saw their own subtle form transform into Baba's form mid-vision, described as reassuring rather than confusing.

Q7. What physical sensations wer e commonly r eported during this practice? A: Per this teaching's live practice, commonly reported sensations included tarang (waves or vibration) through the body , a felt tightening or pressure (one practitioner compared it to sitting in a pressure cooker), sudden fatigue or heaviness, floating or lightness, and eyes closing tightly and involuntarily during intense visions.

Q8. Did Bhaiya confirm the dual-mantra, dual-subtle-body experience as r eal, or was it an individual anomaly? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly confirmed mid-session that many practitioners were independently describing the same real, shared pattern — one side carrying "Jai Siyaram," the other carrying "Ram" — rather than each person imagining something unrelated.

Q9. What did one practitioner (Seema) shar e about being locked in a bathr oom befor e the session? A: Per this teaching's live testimony , Seema described being accidentally locked in a bathroom by her family shortly before the session, praying in distress to be freed in time, and having her daughter unexpectedly open the door at exactly 9:00 — precisely in time for the 9:30 session start — which she of fered as an example of a prayer being answered with striking, literal timing.

Q10. What did the same practitioner observe about Bhaiya's appearance during the session? A: Per this teaching's live testimony , she described continuously perceiving a white-colored aura around Bhaiya throughout the session, which she distinguished from simply the color of his clothing.

Q1 1. Did any practitioners r eport seeing multiple "dimensions" or rapidly shifting scenes? A: Yes — per this teaching's live testimony , at least one practitioner described roughly 12-13 distinct scenes or dimensions witnessed in rapid succession within a single jaap, including visions of Mahishasur , Kali Mata, and Narsimha.

Q12. What did one practitioner from Telangana describe experiencing? A: Per this teaching's live testimony , a practitioner from Telangana described ener gy entering like sunrise through the spine, an invisible subtle form chanting at high speed within an ancient temple setting, and a sensation of the body's ener gy "dividing" until it felt entirely drained — likened to a sudden, significant loss of weight or ener gy .

Q13. Were any pr ocessions of saints (sant) described in this session's visions? A: Yes — per this teaching's live testimony , multiple practitioners described encountering groups of saints, sometimes performing havan, sometimes walking in procession, who invited the practitioner to join them, in some cases leading to a sense of traveling through changing scenes toward a forest ashram.

Q14. How wer e the two subtle bodies typically distinguished fr om each other visually? A: Per this teaching's live testimony , practitioners commonly distinguished their two subtle bodies by color — frequently white, gold, red, or blue — with colors sometimes shifting or blending together as the practice progressed.

Q15. Did any practitioner describe seeing energy or mantra text entering their body dir ectly? A: Yes — per this teaching's live testimony , several practitioners described seeing the words "Jai Siyaram" and "Ram" as visible text entering through their ears, or ener gy entering through the crown of the head, in sync with the mantra being recited.

Q16. What guidance did Bhaiya give about continuing jaap that night, given the Dussehra period? A: Per this teaching, Bhaiya encouraged practitioners to continue their personal jaap into the night as their schedule allowed — up to 12, 1, or 2 a.m. — given the ongoing Dussehra festival, while cautioning against overdoing it to the point of missing the next morning's work or waking obligations.

Q17. Does this session include any individual negativity , pitru, or tantra diagnosis, as in the aura-checking sessions? A: No — per this teaching, this session consists entirely of voluntary , positive meditative experience-sharing rather than individual diagnostic checking, so no privacy-based anonymization was needed for this content.

Q18. What was the practical closing guidance given at the end of this session? A: Per this teaching's closing logistics, practitioners were told to continue jaap for as long as their personal schedule comfortably allowed that night, prioritizing suf ficient rest so as not to compromise the next day's work or responsibilities.
Bot Response Guidelines

Present the visionary/experiential content in this session (portals, deities, dimension-shifting, ener gy visuals) as this tradition's own reported meditative experiences — framed as testimony , not as claims Claude is verifying or endorsing as objective fact. Present the dual-mantra, dual-subtle-body practice (Q1, Q8) as the session's distinctive, confirmed technique, since Bhaiya explicitly validated it as a shared pattern rather than individual imagination. Present the bathroom-lock testimony (Q9) and similar personal answered-prayer accounts with warmth and respect, without amplifying or dramatizing them beyond how they were shared.
